STANDARDS SOURCES (documented repo standards, from AGENTS.md):
1. UI: no raw <div>/<span> for layout (Astryx components only); tokens for every value (var(--color-|--spacing-|--radius-), no raw hex/px in component styling); Card only for dashboard widgets/galleries/settings groups, not list items.
2. Code style: single-statement `if` on one line, no braces (`if (!x) return null`).
3. Prettier: 4-space indent, no semicolons, single quotes, print width 120, no bracket spacing.
4. TypeScript: no inline object types — if a type has more than 2 properties it must be a named type; reuse existing types before creating new ones; don't hand-write types a library exports.
5. Rust: every #[tauri::command] rejects with a coded failure (CommandError or domain error), NEVER Result<_, String>; helper functions deep inside may return plain strings but the command boundary picks the code.
6. Never sleep: no fixed timeouts when an event/condition/retrying assertion is available. Playwright: expect/waitFor/waitForFunction, never page.waitForTimeout. Vitest/RTL: findBy*/waitFor, never setTimeout sleeps. WebdriverIO: waitUntil/waitForDisplayed, never browser.pause. Rust/Node: wait on the event/channel/process; poll only when nothing signals, and then fast with a deadline.
7. Generated surfaces: never hand-edit anything between GENERATED-BEGIN and GENERATED-END markers; a new Godot command needs a catalogue entry in protocol/schemas/v2/commands.json + an addon method; a new desktop command needs lib.rs registration + src/services/desktop.ts types.
8. Agent tools: every tool the model is told about is probed once before a turn — a domain added to CATALOG in src-tauri/src/ai_tools.rs must be answered by probe() in the same file; a new local tool needs a step in WORKSPACE_PROBES in scripts/ai-reachability.mjs.

PLUS the SMELL BASELINE (Fowler, ch.3). Two rules: a documented repo standard overrides the baseline; every smell is a judgement call, never a hard violation. Skip anything tooling (prettier, clippy, tsc) enforces.
- Mysterious Name: name doesn't reveal what it does/holds → rename.
- Duplicated Code: same logic shape in multiple hunks/files → extract shared shape.
- Feature Envy: a method reaches into another object's data more than its own → move it onto that data.
- Data Clumps: same few fields/params travel together → bundle into one type.
- Primitive Obsession: primitive/string standing in for a domain concept → give it its own type.
- Repeated Switches: same switch/if-cascade on the same type recurs → polymorphism or a shared map.
- Shotgun Surgery: one logical change forces scattered edits across many files → gather into one module.
- Divergent Change: one file edited for several unrelated reasons → split.
- Speculative Generality: abstraction/params/hooks for needs the spec doesn't have → delete.
- Message Chains: long a.b().c().d() navigation → hide behind one method.
- Middle Man: class/function mostly delegating onward → cut it.
- Refused Bequest: subclass ignoring most of what it inherits → composition.

BRIEF: Report, per file/hunk where relevant, (a) every place the diff violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule); and (b) any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls: documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls, and a documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words.
